Security hardening across attachment, transport, SSRF, authorization, filter, and OAuth layers (#1448)

* test(security): add xfail-strict regression tests for advisory families

Reproduce known attack vectors and assert the secure outcome, marked
xfail(strict=True) so the suite stays green now and each test auto-flips
(XPASS, forcing marker removal) the moment its root fix lands. Covers HTTP
transport auth bypass (transport 401 + global-credential fallback), SSRF
redirect-hook coverage and backslash parser confusion, projects-filter
bypass on board issues, OAuth token file permissions, and reflected XSS +
JQL injection. Registers a `security_regression` marker for selection.

Every test fails for exactly its asserted security property under
--runxfail, so a passing-as-xfailed false green cannot mask an open
vulnerability.

* fix(security): validate upload attachment file_path against the workspace

The download side gained validate_safe_path (CVE-2026-27825), but the
upload side still fed any caller-supplied file_path to the attachment API
after only an os.path.exists check, so an absolute or ../-traversal path
was read from the server host and exfiltrated. Confine the upload source
to the working directory via validate_safe_path before the file is opened,
in both the Jira and Confluence upload_attachment paths; upload_attachments
and update_issue's attachments param route through the same choke point.

The paired xfail-strict regression tests now XPASS and their markers are
removed, becoming permanent green guards. Existing happy-path upload tests
that mocked os.path.abspath (which neutered the guard) are reworked to
exercise a real in-workspace file.

Closes the upload half of GHSA-wm45-qh3g-v83f, GHSA-vc25-24vv-fxxm,
GHSA-93xw-j965-9mx3, GHSA-6cr4-ccf3-x7h4, GHSA-f4p7-qx46-wc5j,
GHSA-f6pj-qv47-g96w, GHSA-2xj6-xx86-cwwc, GHSA-mrq8-fv7v-hhjg,
GHSA-wv8v-v4c5-v75j, GHSA-p6hp-93wp-fh6p, GHSA-h7wj-5v37-59r2,
GHSA-mfv2-4wvm-9pgp, GHSA-f26r-j276-ggg4, GHSA-9547-j7r6-wj4h, and the
read half of GHSA-cc5h-2pwp-pvcc. The download-side CWD-overwrite variant
(GHSA-6vmq-24h2-pj7j) stays xfail pending the download-dir decision.

* fix(security): gate global-credential fallback behind opt-in for HTTP

An HTTP request with no per-user identity previously fell through to the
operator's global Atlassian credentials at two seams: the transport
middleware proxied it to the app, and _get_fetcher returned a globally
configured fetcher. Any unauthenticated caller on a remotely exposed
streamable-http server therefore transacted as the operator.

Refuse both paths unless ALLOW_GLOBAL_CRED_FALLBACK is explicitly set.
The UserTokenMiddleware now returns 401 for an unauthenticated MCP POST,
and _get_fetcher raises rather than serving the global fetcher in an HTTP
context. Non-HTTP (stdio, single-user) is unchanged, so the default
quickstart keeps working; single-user HTTP deployments opt in with the flag.

The paired xfail-strict regression tests now XPASS and their markers are
removed. The companion global-fallback tests that pinned the old HTTP
behavior are updated to opt in.

Closes GHSA-wrhw-j3f9-8vc6, GHSA-vc8m-84rp-53hx, and the auth half of
GHSA-cc5h-2pwp-pvcc.

* fix(security): attach SSRF redirect hook on all per-user auth branches

The SSRF redirect hook was attached only on the header-PAT branch of the
per-user fetcher resolution; the basic-auth and OAuth/PAT branches built
sessions with no redirect validation, so a per-user fetcher followed HTTP
redirects to internal/metadata hosts without the SSRF guard. Pass
attach_ssrf_hook=True on those branches too.

The paired xfail-strict regression tests (basic and OAuth, Jira and
Confluence) now XPASS and their markers are removed.

Closes GHSA-6529-c226-h328.

* fix(security): write OAuth token fallback file owner-only (0o600)

The OAuth token fallback file (~/.mcp-atlassian/oauth-<client_id>.json)
was written with the process umask and no explicit mode, so on a typical
0o022 umask it landed group/world-readable — persisting long-lived
refresh/access tokens as readable secrets. Create and truncate it via
os.open with 0o600 (and chmod the containing directory to 0o700),
independent of the umask.

The paired xfail-strict regression test now XPASS and its marker is
removed; the existing save test is reworked to write a real temp file.

Closes GHSA-g5xv-mhgm-v5f6, GHSA-76pr-5669-3xf5, GHSA-4596-2p6p-28cv.

* fix(security): HTML-escape the OAuth callback message (reflected XSS)

The local OAuth setup callback server interpolated the response message
straight into the HTML body. The message includes attacker-controllable
text from the callback (e.g. the OAuth error query parameter), so a
crafted authorize redirect reflected executable markup into the page.
Escape the message with html.escape before rendering.

The paired xfail-strict regression test now XPASS and its marker is removed.

Closes GHSA-g2r2-3j32-j27x.

* fix(security): apply projects filter to board issues; require numeric sprint_id

Two Jira search bypasses:

- get_board_issues never applied config.projects_filter, so board queries
  escaped the JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER allowlist. Extract the filter logic from
  search_issues into a shared _apply_projects_filter helper and route both
  search and board issues through it, so no JQL path can skip the allowlist.

- get_sprint_issues interpolated sprint_id straight into JQL
  (f"sprint = {sprint_id}"), so a non-numeric value injected JQL. Require an
  integer.

The paired xfail-strict regression tests now XPASS and their markers are removed.

Closes the board-issues filter bypass (GHSA-w66g-j6c4-hcfc,
GHSA-rqwg-9346-fjjv) and the sprint JQL-injection half of GHSA-6rrj-86cw-gg9j.

* fix(security): reject backslash authority-confusion in SSRF validation

validate_url_for_ssrf extracted the host with urlparse().hostname, but
requests (and browsers, per WHATWG) treat a backslash in the authority as
a path separator. So "http://localhost\@evil.com/" validates as host
evil.com (external, allowed) yet actually connects to localhost — an SSRF
bypass of the guard. Reject any URL whose authority contains a backslash.

The paired xfail-strict regression test now XPASS and its marker is removed.

Closes GHSA-hgcf-4mq8-5266.

* fix(security): validate redirects for SSRF on every client session

The SSRF redirect hook was attached only to per-user HTTP fetchers via
_create_and_validate, so global/stdio fetchers and direct
self.jira._session.get() calls (jira/development.py, jira/users.py) followed
redirects with no SSRF validation. Attach the hook once at base-client
construction (Jira and Confluence) so every outbound request is covered.

Adds a regression test asserting the base session carries the hook and blocks
a redirect to the cloud-metadata address.

Closes GHSA-v9m3-wfh8-5646 and GHSA-5wf4-jqxh-8gm3.

* fix(security): always AND the project/space allowlist (no caller bypass)

The Jira projects-filter and Confluence spaces-filter were skipped whenever
the caller's query already named a project/space ("only add if not already
filtering"). So a caller-supplied `project = EVIL` / `space = EVIL` escaped
JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER / CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER entirely. Always AND the
configured allowlist instead: legitimate in-allowlist narrowing is redundant
but valid, and an out-of-allowlist query now returns empty (correctly denied).
A trailing ORDER BY is extracted so the AND stays valid JQL/CQL.

Adds security-regression tests pinning the no-bypass property; existing tests
that asserted the old skip behavior are updated to the secure semantics.

Deepens the fix for GHSA-w66g-j6c4-hcfc and GHSA-rqwg-9346-fjjv (the
caller-supplied-clause bypass sub-bug, beyond board issues).

* fix(security): make the configured project/space allowlist a hard boundary

The projects_filter / spaces_filter tool arguments used `arg or config`, so a
caller could pass projects_filter="SECRET" to drop the operator's configured
JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER / CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER allowlist entirely — defeating
the allowlist in exactly the shared-credential deployments the auth gate
protects. Apply the configured allowlist unconditionally as a boundary and
treat the tool argument as an additional narrowing (both are ANDed): a caller
can restrict within the allowlist but never escape it.

Adds security-regression tests pinning "arg cannot replace config"; existing
tests that asserted arg-overrides-config are updated to the narrowing semantics.

Hardens GHSA-w66g-j6c4-hcfc / GHSA-rqwg-9346-fjjv (found by adversarial review
of the prior always-AND fix).

* fix(security): enforce ENABLED_TOOLS/toolset authorization at call time

_list_tools_mcp filtered the tool listing by ENABLED_TOOLS, enabled toolsets,
and read-only mode, but the call path (_call_tool_mcp) did not re-check — so a
client that knew a tool's name could invoke a tool that was excluded from the
listing (disabled toolset, not in the ENABLED_TOOLS allowlist, or a write tool
in read-only mode), bypassing the operator's toolset authorization.

Factor the authorization decision into _is_tool_authorized (ENABLED_TOOLS +
toolset + read-only) shared by both listing and calling, and override
_call_tool_mcp to deny unauthorized tools with the same "Unknown tool" error as
a nonexistent one (no exists-but-disabled leak). Service availability stays a
listing-only graceful-hide (an unconfigured-service tool fails naturally).

Adds a dispatch-level regression test proving a denied call never reaches the
executor and an authorized call does (guards against FastMCP-isolation
false-greens).

Closes GHSA-3r68-hf9h-887v.

* fix(security): refuse attachment downloads into the working-directory root

download_attachment validated against path traversal but still allowed writing
into the CWD root (validate_safe_path's default base_dir), where Python resolves
imports first — so a download could overwrite an importable module and gain code
execution. Refuse targets whose parent directory is the CWD itself; attachments
must be saved into a subdirectory (download_issue_attachments already uses one).

The paired xfail-strict regression test now XPASS and its marker is removed;
existing download happy-path tests are updated to target a subdirectory.

Closes GHSA-6vmq-24h2-pj7j.

* fix(security): pin DNS resolution to close SSRF rebinding (validate→connect TOCTOU)

validate_url_for_ssrf resolves and checks a host once (in middleware), but the
outbound request re-resolves at connect time, so a DNS-rebinding response can
return a public IP to the check and a private/metadata IP to the connection —
bypassing the SSRF guard on the patched build.

Add SsrfPinningAdapter: a requests transport adapter whose connection resolves
each host exactly once, rejects any candidate address that is not globally
routable, and connects to that same validated address. There is no second
resolution to rebind. The hostname is preserved for TLS SNI and certificate
verification, so HTTPS is unaffected. Mounted on the Jira and Confluence client
sessions, preserving each client's existing retry policy.

Verified: rebind to a metadata IP is refused end-to-end through the real
requests/urllib3 stack; a real HTTPS request still succeeds (cert-verified, SNI
preserved); the resolved IP is the one connected to (single getaddrinfo).
Recommend a Cloud/DC e2e pass to confirm proxy/real-instance interaction before
disclosure.

Closes GHSA-49xv-9743-pw8w, GHSA-72fm-whvq-jghf, GHSA-489g-7rxv-6c8q.

* tests: describe security regressions by GHSA id

* tests(confluence): upload uses POST since #1253, not PUT

* style: sort imports (ruff)

* style: ruff-format + mypy stubs for the SSRF pinning adapter

* fix(security): confine content_file reads to the workspace

The content_file parameter added by #1275 read any caller-supplied path
(expanduser + read_text) and echoed it into the created/updated page —
the same arbitrary-file-read class as the attachment-path advisories.
Route it through validate_safe_path.

e2e: attachment/content_file fixtures now write inside the workspace
(new workspace_tmp_path fixture) to match the confinement contract.

* fix(security): exempt operator-configured hosts from SSRF non-global rejection

The DNS-pinning adapter rejected every non-global resolution, which broke
on-prem DC deployments outright (private-network or localhost base URLs)
whenever ssl_verify was on — and with ssl_verify off, the domain-specific
SSLIgnoreAdapter silently replaced the pinning adapter entirely (requests
picks the longest mount prefix), dropping the rebinding guard.

- Waive the non-global rejection for hosts from JIRA_URL / CONFLUENCE_URL
  and MCP_ALLOWED_URL_DOMAINS: server-environment values an attacker cannot
  reach through a request. Caller-supplied hosts are still rejected, and the
  single-resolution pin applies to every host.
- SSLIgnoreAdapter now carries the pinned connection classes, so disabling
  certificate verification no longer disables the SSRF guard.

* test(e2e): export DC base URLs as env so the SSRF pin trusts the harness hosts

* fix: apply HTTP hardening after the SSRF pinning mount so send wrappers survive

configure_concurrency/rate_limit/circuit_breaker patch adapter.send in
place on whatever adapters are mounted at call time; mount_ssrf_pinning
replaces the generic http/https adapters (carrying over only
max_retries), so running the hardening first silently dropped its send
wrappers. Mount the pinning adapter first, then harden. Regression test
covers the ordering.

* docs: caller project/space filters narrow the configured allowlist, not override it

The hard-boundary commit changed the semantics but left the Args
docstrings claiming the caller filter 'overrides config'.

* test(attachments): pin workspace in upload happy-path tests for py3.13

The upload-mechanics tests fed an out-of-workspace absolute path and
relied on mocking os.path.abspath to neutralize validate_safe_path. On
Python 3.13 pathlib.Path.resolve() no longer routes through os.path.abspath,
so the real guard rejected the path and the tests failed. Pin os.getcwd to
the path's parent so it resolves inside the workspace and the guard passes
legitimately on all versions. The guard itself stays covered by the
mock-free security_regression suite.

+"""A requests transport adapter that pins DNS resolution against SSRF.
+
+``validate_url_for_ssrf`` resolves and checks a host once (in middleware), but the
+outbound request re-resolves the hostname at connect time, so a DNS-rebinding
+response can swap in an internal address between validation and connection — the
+TOCTOU that bypasses a validate-then-reconnect SSRF guard (GHSA-49xv, 72fm, 489g).
+
+This adapter closes that window at the connection itself: it resolves each host
+exactly once, rejects any candidate address that is not globally routable
+(cloud-metadata / private / loopback), and connects to that same validated
+address — there is no separate re-resolution to rebind. The original hostname is
+preserved for TLS SNI and certificate verification, so HTTPS is unaffected.
+
+Operator-trusted hosts — the configured ``JIRA_URL`` / ``CONFLUENCE_URL`` hosts
+and ``MCP_ALLOWED_URL_DOMAINS`` entries — are exempt from the non-global
+rejection (on-prem DC instances legitimately live on private networks or
+localhost). Those values come from the server environment, which an attacker
+cannot influence through a request, so the rebinding guard is not weakened for
+caller-supplied URLs. The single-resolution pin still applies to every host.
+"""
+
+import os
+import socket
+from typing import Any
+from urllib.parse import urlparse
+
+from requests import Session
+from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
+from urllib3.connection import HTTPConnection, HTTPSConnection
+from urllib3.connectionpool import HTTPConnectionPool, HTTPSConnectionPool
+from urllib3.exceptions import NewConnectionError
+from urllib3.poolmanager import PoolManager
+
+from .urls import _check_ip_address, _get_domain_allowlist, _hostname_matches_allowlist
+
+
+def _operator_trusted_hosts() -> list[str]:
+    """Hosts the operator explicitly configured or allowlisted via environment."""
+    hosts = []
+    for env in ("JIRA_URL", "CONFLUENCE_URL"):
+        raw = os.environ.get(env, "").strip()
+        if raw:
+            hostname = urlparse(raw).hostname
+            if hostname:
+                hosts.append(hostname.lower())
+    hosts.extend(_get_domain_allowlist() or [])
+    return hosts
+
+
+def _pinned_create_connection(
+    address: tuple[str, int],
+    timeout: Any = socket._GLOBAL_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,  # type: ignore[attr-defined]  # noqa: SLF001
+    source_address: tuple[str, int] | None = None,
+    socket_options: Any = None,
+) -> socket.socket:
+    """Resolve once, reject non-global addresses, connect to the validated IP.
+
+    A single ``getaddrinfo`` result is both validated and connected to, so a
+    rebinding name cannot return a public IP to the check and a private IP to the
+    connection.
+    """
+    host, port = address
+    host_trusted = _hostname_matches_allowlist(host, _operator_trusted_hosts())
+    err: Exception | None = None
+    for af, socktype, proto, _canonname, sa in socket.getaddrinfo(
+        host, port, 0, socket.SOCK_STREAM
+    ):
+        ip = sa[0]
+        if not host_trusted and _check_ip_address(ip) is not None:
+            msg = f"SSRF blocked: {host} resolves to non-global address {ip}"
+            raise OSError(msg)
+        sock = None
+        try:
+            sock = socket.socket(af, socktype, proto)
+            if socket_options:
+                for opt in socket_options:
+                    sock.setsockopt(*opt)
+            if timeout is not socket._GLOBAL_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT:  # type: ignore[attr-defined]  # noqa: SLF001
+                sock.settimeout(timeout)
+            if source_address:
+                sock.bind(source_address)
+            sock.connect(sa)
+            return sock
+        except OSError as e:
+            err = e
+            if sock is not None:
+                sock.close()
+    if err is not None:
+        raise err
+    msg = f"getaddrinfo returned no addresses for {host}"
+    raise OSError(msg)
+
+
+class _PinnedConnMixin:
+    """Route socket creation through the validating, single-resolution connector."""
+
+    def _new_conn(self) -> socket.socket:
+        try:
+            return _pinned_create_connection(
+                (self._dns_host, self.port),  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+                self.timeout,  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+                source_address=self.source_address,  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+                socket_options=self.socket_options,  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+            )
+        except OSError as e:
+            raise NewConnectionError(
+                self,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+                f"Failed to establish a new connection: {e}",
+            ) from e
+
+
+class _PinnedHTTPConnection(_PinnedConnMixin, HTTPConnection):
+    pass
+
+
+class _PinnedHTTPSConnection(_PinnedConnMixin, HTTPSConnection):
+    pass
+
+
+class _PinnedHTTPConnectionPool(HTTPConnectionPool):
+    ConnectionCls = _PinnedHTTPConnection
+
+
+class _PinnedHTTPSConnectionPool(HTTPSConnectionPool):
+    ConnectionCls = _PinnedHTTPSConnection
+
+
+class SsrfPinningAdapter(HTTPAdapter):
+    """A requests adapter that validates and pins DNS resolution for every call."""
+
+    def init_poolmanager(
+        self, connections: int, maxsize: int, block: bool = False, **pool_kwargs: Any
+    ) -> None:
+        self.poolmanager = PoolManager(
+            num_pools=connections, maxsize=maxsize, block=block, **pool_kwargs
+        )
+        # Runtime attribute of urllib3's PoolManager; absent from the type stubs.
+        self.poolmanager.pool_classes_by_scheme = {  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+            "http": _PinnedHTTPConnectionPool,
+            "https": _PinnedHTTPSConnectionPool,
+        }
+
+
+def mount_ssrf_pinning(session: Session) -> None:
+    """Mount the SSRF DNS-pinning adapter for http/https on ``session``.
+
+    Preserves the retry policy of any adapter already mounted (e.g. the one the
+    Atlassian client configures), so pinning does not silently drop retries.
+    """
+    for scheme in ("https://", "http://"):
+        existing = session.adapters.get(scheme)
+        retries = getattr(existing, "max_retries", None)
+        adapter = (
+            SsrfPinningAdapter(max_retries=retries)
+            if retries is not None
+            else SsrfPinningAdapter()
+        )
+        session.mount(scheme, adapter)

+"""Regression tests for the SSRF DNS-pinning transport adapter (DNS rebinding).
+
+These cover GHSA-49xv, GHSA-72fm, GHSA-489g: the validate-then-reconnect TOCTOU
+where a rebinding host returns a public IP to ``validate_url_for_ssrf`` and a
+private/metadata IP to the actual connection. The adapter resolves once, validates
+that resolution, and connects to the same address — so there is no second
+resolution to rebind.
+"""
+
+import socket
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import pytest
+import requests
+
+from mcp_atlassian.utils.ssrf_adapter import (
+    SsrfPinningAdapter,
+    _pinned_create_connection,
+)
+
+
+def _gai_returning(ip: str):
+    def gai(host, port, *args, **kwargs):
+        return [(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM, 6, "", (ip, port or 443))]
+
+    return gai
+
+
+@pytest.mark.security_regression
+def test_rebind_internal_address_refused_with_single_resolution():
+    """A host resolving to a non-global address is refused, after exactly one
+    resolution — the resolved address is the one that would be connected to."""
+    calls = {"n": 0}
+
+    def gai(host, port, *args, **kwargs):
+        calls["n"] += 1
+        return [(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM, 6, "", ("169.254.169.254", 443))]
+
+    with patch("mcp_atlassian.utils.ssrf_adapter.socket.getaddrinfo", side_effect=gai):
+        with pytest.raises(OSError, match="non-global"):
+            _pinned_create_connection(("rebind.attacker.test", 443))
+
+    assert calls["n"] == 1
+
+
+@pytest.mark.security_regression
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("ip", ["169.254.169.254", "127.0.0.1", "10.0.0.5", "::1"])
+def test_pinning_adapter_blocks_internal_through_real_stack(ip):
+    """End-to-end through the mounted adapter and the real requests/urllib3 stack:
+    a host resolving to an internal address is refused — proving the adapter is
+    actually wired into the connection path (not a mock-only green)."""
+    session = requests.Session()
+    session.mount("https://", SsrfPinningAdapter())
+    session.mount("http://", SsrfPinningAdapter())
+
+    with patch(
+        "mcp_atlassian.utils.ssrf_adapter.socket.getaddrinfo",
+        side_effect=_gai_returning(ip),
+    ):
+        with pytest.raises(requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, match="SSRF blocked"):
+            session.get("https://rebind.attacker.test", timeout=5)
+
+
+class _FakeConnectSock:
+    def __init__(self, connected):
+        self._connected = connected
+
+    def setsockopt(self, *a):
+        pass
+
+    def settimeout(self, *a):
+        pass
+
+    def bind(self, *a):
+        pass
+
+    def connect(self, sa):
+        self._connected["addr"] = sa
+
+    def close(self):
+        pass
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "env",
+    [
+        {"JIRA_URL": "http://jira.internal:8080"},
+        {"CONFLUENCE_URL": "https://jira.internal/wiki"},
+        {"MCP_ALLOWED_URL_DOMAINS": "jira.internal"},
+    ],
+)
+def test_operator_configured_host_may_resolve_private(env, monkeypatch):
+    """The operator-configured base host (or an allowlisted domain) may live on a
+    private network — the non-global rejection is waived, but the connection is
+    still pinned to the single resolved address."""

+        monkeypatch.delenv(k, raising=False)

+
+    with (
+        patch(
+            "mcp_atlassian.utils.ssrf_adapter.socket.getaddrinfo",
+            side_effect=_gai_returning("10.0.0.5"),

+            "mcp_atlassian.utils.ssrf_adapter.socket.socket",

+    pinning adapter (requests picks the longest prefix), so it must carry the
+    pinned connection classes itself — otherwise ssl_verify=false silently
+    disables the SSRF rebinding guard."""
+    from mcp_atlassian.utils.ssl import SSLIgnoreAdapter

+    monkeypatch.delenv("JIRA_URL", raising=False)

+        side_effect=_gai_returning("169.254.169.254"),
+    ):
+        with pytest.raises(requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, match="SSRF blocked"):
+            session.get("http://rebind.attacker.test", timeout=5)

+class TestSsrfBackslashBypassRegression:
+    """Regression (GHSA-hgcf) — backslash authority-confusion SSRF bypass.
+
+    ``validate_url_for_ssrf`` extracts the host via ``urlparse().hostname``
+    (``urls.py:92``), but ``requests`` (and browsers) parse a backslash in the
+    authority differently: ``urlparse("http://localhost\\@evil.com/").hostname`` is
+    ``"evil.com"`` (external, so validation passes), while ``requests`` connects to
+    ``localhost`` / ``127.0.0.1`` — the validator would approve a URL that
+    actually targets an internal host. These tests assert the secure outcome: the
+    backslash-confusion URL is blocked.
+    """
+
+    @pytest.mark.security_regression
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        "url",
+        ["http://localhost\\@evil.com/", "http://127.0.0.1\\@evil.com/"],
+        ids=["localhost-backslash", "loopback-ip-backslash"],
+    )
+    @patch.dict(os.environ, {"MCP_ALLOWED_URL_DOMAINS": ""})
+    @patch("mcp_atlassian.utils.urls.socket.getaddrinfo")
+    def test_backslash_authority_confusion_is_blocked(
+        self, mock_getaddrinfo, url: str
+    ) -> None:
+        """A URL whose parsed host disagrees with its connection target is blocked."""
+        # DNS mock: evil.com resolves to a GLOBAL IP, so the *bare* host is "safe".
+        # This isolates the block to backslash normalization, not a DNS failure.
+        mock_getaddrinfo.return_value = [
+            (socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM, 6, "", ("93.184.216.34", 0))
+        ]
+        # Sanity: the external host on its own passes validation under this mock.
+        assert validate_url_for_ssrf("http://evil.com/") is None
+        # The backslash-confusion URL parses to evil.com but really targets internal.
+        result = validate_url_for_ssrf(url)
+        assert result is not None, (
+            "URL with backslash authority confusion must be blocked — the parsed "
+            "host disagrees with the real connection target"
+        )
